items.title: 2.10.3 Method to Find Global Extrema of a Continuous Functions Defined on a Closed Interval [a, b] (Roman Urdu)

source_refs.note: Book p. 54: 2.10.3 three-step method for global extrema on [a, b], Example 20 (derivative misprinted as x^4 - 4x)

blocks.text: Ab hum ek aisa tareeqa seekhte hain jo har us function par chalta hai jo closed interval \([a, b]\) par continuous ho (yani graph beech mein kahin toota na ho). Sawal hota hai: is interval mein function ki sab se bari aur sab se chhoti value kya hai? Jawab teen aasaan steps mein mil jata hai. Yeh bilkul aise hai jaise kisi race ke winner ko dhoondna: pehle sirf un logon ki list banao jo jeet sakte hain, phir un ka muqabla karo.

items: Interval \([a, b]\) ke andar function ke tamaam critical points nikaalein.
Critical points aur interval ke end points par function ki values nikaalein.
In values mein sab se bari global maximum value hai aur sab se chhoti global minimum value.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Sirf yahi points kyun? Closed interval par continuous function ka global maximum aur global minimum zaroor hota hai (2.10.2). Agar yeh interval ke andar kahin aaye to wahan graph mur raha hota hai, yani woh critical point hota hai; warna woh kisi end point par aata hai. Is liye "umeedwar" (candidates) sirf do qisam ke hain: \([a, b]\) ke andar ke critical points aur do end points \(a\) aur \(b\).
Har umeedwar ke baare mein alag se yeh faisla karne ki zaroorat nahin ke woh maximum hai ya minimum; bas values ka muqabla kar lijiye. Sab se aasaan aur sab se mehfooz tareeqa.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Do sharten kyun lagai gayin, closed interval aur continuous? Dono mein se ek bhi na ho to extrema gum ho sakte hain:
1. \(f(x) = x\), open interval \((0, 1)\) par: values 0 ke qareeb aur 1 ke qareeb jati hain magar kabhi 0 ya 1 nahin banti, kyun ke end points shamil hi nahin. Na sab se bari value hai na sab se chhoti.
2. \(f(x) = \frac{1}{x}\), \([-1, 1]\) par (0 ke ilawa): 0 ke paas graph toot jata hai aur values bina had ke oopar aur neeche jati hain. Koi global maximum ya minimum nahin.
Is liye tareeqa lagane se pehle hamesha dekh lijiye ke interval band (closed) hai aur function us par bina toote (continuous) hai. Polynomials har jagah continuous hote hain, is liye un mein yeh fikr nahin.

blocks.title: Example 20
blocks.problem: Find the global extreme values of \(f(x) = x^{4} - 4x\) on \([-2, 3]\).
steps:
Diya gaya: \(f(x) = x^{4} - 4x\) ...(1), closed interval \([-2, 3]\) par.
Maloom karna: global maximum aur global minimum values.
Tareeqa: upar wala teen step ka tareeqa. \(f\) polynomial hai, is liye \([-2, 3]\) par continuous hai; is ke global extrema critical points aur end points ki values mein se hi honge.

Step 1: Equation (1) ka derivative
\[f'(x) = 4x^{3} - 4 \quad \text{...(2)}\]
Kyun: power rule: \(\frac{d}{dx}(x^{4}) = 4x^{3}\) aur \(\frac{d}{dx}(4x) = 4\).
Dhyan dein: kitab yahan ghalti se \(f'(x)\) ki jagah dobara \(x^{4} - 4x\) chhaap deti hai (neeche "Kitab ki ghalti"); agli line mein woh sahi \(4x^{3} - 4\) hi use karti hai.

Step 2: Critical points
Equation (2) se saaf hai ke \(f'(x)\) poore \([-2, 3]\) par exist karta hai. Stationary points ke liye \(f'(x) = 0\):
\[4x^{3} - 4 = 0\]
\[4(x^{3} - 1) = 0\]
\[(x - 1)(x^{2} + x + 1) = 0\]
Kyun: cubes ka farq (difference of cubes): \(x^{3} - 1 = (x - 1)(x^{2} + x + 1)\). 4 ko dono taraf divide kar diya kyun ke woh zero nahin.

Step 3: Sirf real roots
Ya \(x - 1 = 0\) ya \(x^{2} + x + 1 = 0\). Doosri equation ka discriminant \(1 - 4 = -3 < 0\) hai, is liye us ke roots complex hain. To akela real stationary point \(x = 1\) hai, aur yeh \([-2, 3]\) ke andar hai.
Kyun: graph sirf real numbers par banta hai; complex root graph par koi point nahin deta.

Step 4: Critical point aur end points par values
\[f(1) = 1^{4} - 4(1) = -3\]
\[f(-2) = (-2)^{4} - 4(-2) = 16 + 8 = 24\]
\[f(3) = 3^{4} - 4(3) = 81 - 12 = 69\]
Kyun: tareeqe ka step 2: end points ko kabhi mat bhooliye.
Dhyan dein: \((-2)^{4} = +16\) aur \(-4(-2) = +8\); dono plus hain.

Step 5: Muqabla
Values \(-3\), \(24\), \(69\) mein sab se bari 69 aur sab se chhoti \(-3\) hai.
Kyun: tareeqe ka step 3.

Tasdeeq: \(x < 1\) par \(f'(x) < 0\) aur \(x > 1\) par \(f'(x) > 0\) (misaal: \(f'(0) = -4\), \(f'(2) = 28\)). Yani \(f\) pehle 24 se \(-3\) tak girta hai aur phir 69 tak uthta hai. Sab se neecha point \(x = 1\) par aur sab se ooncha right end \(x = 3\) par: jawab sahi hai.
blocks.answer: Global maximum \(f(3) = 69\) hai aur global minimum \(f(1) = -3\) hai.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Example 20 mein kitab derivative ko \(f'(x) = x^{4} - 4x\) ...(2) chhaapti hai, jo asal mein \(f(x)\) hi dobara likh diya gaya hai. Sahi derivative \(f'(x) = 4x^{3} - 4\) hai. Agli line (\(4x^{3} - 4 = 0\)) aur aakhri jawab sahi derivative se hi bane hain.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
\(f(x) = x^{2} - 2x\), interval \([0, 3]\) par.
\(f'(x) = 2x - 2 = 0\) se \(x = 1\), jo interval ke andar hai.
Values: \(f(1) = -1\), \(f(0) = 0\), \(f(3) = 9 - 6 = 3\).
Muqabla: global maximum \(f(3) = 3\) (end point par), global minimum \(f(1) = -1\) (critical point par).

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: Agar Example 20 mein interval \([-2, 3]\) ke bajaye \([2, 3]\) hota to kya badalta? (Jawab: critical point \(x = 1\) ab interval se bahar hai, is liye use chhor dete. Sirf end points bachte: \(f(2) = 16 - 8 = 8\), \(f(3) = 69\). Global minimum 8 aur global maximum 69.)

blocks.title: Exam tip
blocks.text: Umeedwaron ko ek line mein likhiye: "Critical point value: \(f(1) = -3\); end point values: \(f(-2) = 24\), \(f(3) = 69\)". Phir global maximum aur minimum un ke points ke saath likhiye. Saaf tarteeb se poore marks milte hain.

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. \([a, b]\) par global extrema ke umeedwar: andar ke critical points aur end points \(a\), \(b\).
2. Har umeedwar par \(f\) ki value nikaalo; sab se bari = global maximum value, sab se chhoti = global minimum value.
3. Interval se bahar wale critical points aur complex roots chhor do.
4. Example 20: global maximum \(f(3) = 69\), global minimum \(f(1) = -3\).

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. End points bhool jana: Example 20 mein global maximum end point \(x = 3\) par hai.
2. Values nikaalte waqt critical point ko \(f\) ke bajaye \(f'\) mein rakh dena (\(f'\) to wahan zero hi aayega).
3. Interval se bahar wale critical point ko bhi shamil kar lena.
